_about: The voice quality test, round 2 (tools/voice-styles.py). Round 1's picks (voice-source/burger-bar-voice-picks.json, 2026-11-08) approved Mitch and sent Marge, Gus, Coach Bev and Vernon back for new voices with the notes quoted in 'asked'; Sal is new. Each style is a Voice Studio 'Describe a voice' description (VoxCPM2: who, how it sounds, how it speaks; no rasp or gravel words, which came out as distortion in round 1). sample: what the designed voice says (the clip every game line is then cloned from). line: the game line the test plays; the voice model is given it with the recorder's own respellings from tools/voices.json (Marge's 'hun', Coach Bev's calm punctuation), or 'say' if a character has one. pitch (Hz) and rate (words a second): what a candidate should roughly land on.

marge.name: Marge
marge.asked: Deliver on hon with comma sounds unnatural. it's still distorted. let's reprompt with some different styles to choose from.
marge.line: It's fine, hon. I was married forty years. I know fine.
marge.sample: Hi, hun. The usual, please. You know how I like it, and I know you'll get it right.

styles.label: Sweet grandma
styles.describe: An elderly woman around seventy, a retired school-bus driver. A warm, smooth, gentle voice, medium pitch. Unhurried, sweet and kind, with a dry, knowing sense of humor. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Southern charm
styles.describe: An elderly woman around seventy from Georgia with a light Southern accent. A warm, smooth, honeyed voice. Sweet, unhurried and gently teasing. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Brassy and dry
styles.describe: An older woman around seventy, a no-nonsense retired bus driver. A clear, confident, brassy voice. Dry, deadpan and wisecracking, but warm underneath. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Chatty Midwest
styles.describe: A cheerful elderly woman around seventy from Minnesota with a Midwestern accent. A bright, friendly, clear voice. Chatty, polite and sweet as pie. Clear studio recording.

gus.name: Gus
gus.asked: needs more western drawl and slightly faster cadence
gus.line: It'll do, buddy. I've eaten worse at truck stops. Way worse.
gus.sample: Howdy, buddy. Eleven hours of highway behind me, and I'm hungry enough to eat the steering wheel.

styles.label: Texas drawl
styles.describe: A big, friendly long-haul trucker around fifty with a heavy Texas accent and a Western drawl. A deep, warm voice. Easygoing and friendly, at an easy, steady pace. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Southern drawl
styles.describe: A big, burly trucker around fifty from Tennessee with a heavy Southern drawl. A deep, warm, friendly voice. Relaxed but lively, at a steady pace. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Cowboy
styles.describe: A weathered cowboy around fifty from Wyoming with a Western drawl. A low, warm, friendly voice. Laid-back and good-humored, but not slow. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Country
styles.describe: A friendly country trucker around fifty from Oklahoma with a heavy country accent. A deep, warm, rumbling voice. Chatty and good-natured, at a natural pace. Clear studio recording.

bev.name: Coach Bev
bev.asked: too high pitch. distorted. needs a butch female sounding character.
bev.line: Hustle, hustle! I've got practice in twenty!
bev.sample: Alright, listen up. I want a double cheeseburger, medium. And I want it like we're down by six in the fourth quarter.
bev._first_try: The first wording (loud, barks orders, cheering, an all-exclamation sample) shouted at 209-393 Hz with clarity down to 2.3: the 'too high, distorted' of round 1 again. These ask for a low-pitched voice speaking steadily.

styles.label: Butch coach
styles.describe: A tough, butch woman in her forties, a high-school gym coach. A low-pitched, deep voice for a woman, almost masculine. Firm, blunt and no-nonsense, speaking steadily rather than shouting. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Drill sergeant
styles.describe: A burly, muscular woman in her forties, a retired army drill sergeant who now coaches gym. A deep, low-pitched, powerful alto voice. Firm and intense, but calm. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Softball coach
styles.describe: A stocky woman softball coach in her forties. A deep, low-pitched alto voice, confident and gruff. Matter-of-fact and competitive. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Boston coach
styles.describe: A tough woman gym coach in her forties from Boston with a Boston accent. A low-pitched, deep voice. Blunt and competitive, talking steadily. Clear studio recording.

vernon.name: Vernon
vernon.asked: this character needs to have a foppish fem male voice similar to Frasier or his brother niles.
vernon.line: [sigh] Ah. You again. My eleven followers are waiting.
vernon.sample: Good evening. I'll be reviewing tonight. The bun, the patty, the presentation. My readers expect nothing less.

styles.label: Fussy snob
styles.describe: A fussy, foppish man around forty, a snobbish food blogger. A light, refined tenor voice with crisp, precise, over-enunciated diction and a haughty, slightly nasal tone. Prissy and pompous. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Effete and theatrical
styles.describe: An effete, delicate, upper-class man around forty. A soft, light, airy voice, theatrical and easily offended, savouring every word. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Mid-Atlantic
styles.describe: A pompous, over-educated man around forty with a polished mid-Atlantic accent. A smooth, refined tenor voice, precise and fastidious, every word chosen with great care. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Prissy and high-strung
styles.describe: A prim, high-strung, finicky man around forty. A thin, slightly high, nasal voice, fluttery and dramatic, fussing over every detail. Clear studio recording.

sal.name: Sal
sal.asked: add a character like Carl from aqua teen with a similar new york gruff crude speaking style
sal.line: Ay. Twelve hours sellin' hot dogs. You know what's in a hot dog? I do. That's why I'm here.
sal.sample: Yo. I been standin' at that hot dog cart since six in the mornin', and my feet are killin' me. Gimme a burger.
sal._first_try: The first wording (loud, brash, loud-mouthed, pushy) came out shouting at 170-310 Hz; only 1 of 16 sounded like a deep, gruff man. These ask for low-pitched grumbling instead.

styles.label: The Bronx
styles.describe: A heavyset man in his fifties from the Bronx with a heavy New York accent. A low-pitched, deep, gruff voice. Blunt, grumpy and crude, grumbling rather than shouting. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Brooklyn
styles.describe: A big, burly hot-dog vendor in his fifties from Brooklyn with a thick Brooklyn accent. A deep, low-pitched, chesty voice. Sarcastic and grumpy, talking out of the side of his mouth. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Queens
styles.describe: A grouchy, heavyset man around sixty from Queens, New York, with a strong New York accent. A deep, low, gruff voice. Impatient and wisecracking, in a gruff mutter. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Jersey
styles.describe: A heavyset, crude man in his fifties from New Jersey with a heavy New Jersey accent. A deep, low-pitched voice. Lazy, cranky and blunt. Clear studio recording.
